_expect.name: West Ridge - part E - top to Xanadu

co_west_ridge_part_e_top_to_xanadu.blurb: The highest and airiest stretch of the West Ridge in Eldorado Canyon, running up to the end of the ridge near Xanadu. It is almost entirely traditional climbing on sandstone, in one to three pitch outings on a ridge that looks out over the canyon. Grades cluster from 5.9 to 5.11, with 5.10 the largest group, and Chockstone, Laughing at the Moon and Prince of Darkness are the names to know. The walk-in is long and a little adventurous, and some loose rock remains, so a helmet is worth wearing. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons; summer works best early in the day.
co_west_ridge_part_e_top_to_xanadu.approach: Count on half an hour or more. From the west end of the park, follow the canyon trail to the Rincon and pick a way up the talus. Other ways in cross the creek from Milton Boulder or come in from the east end over a slippery third-class ramp.

co_middle_mother_s.blurb: Middle Mother's is the home of Unaweep Canyon's steep, technical one-pitch granite, much of it 5.10 and 5.11 with 5.11 the biggest share. Nearly all of it is trad, with a few bolted lines, and the cracks and crimpy faces reward careful gear placement. Iron Maiden, Jagged Edge, Dirty Harry and Alacrity are among the standouts. The buttress falls into shade in the late afternoon, which makes it a decent choice when the canyon is warm. Spring and fall are the best times to visit.
co_middle_mother_s.parking_note: Turn off Highway 141 into the Mother's Buttress trailhead lot, a short drive west of the Sunday Wall pullout, and follow the trail from there.

co_dome_the_2.blurb: The Dome is a big granite slab on the side of Boulder Canyon, cut by cracks and ledges and close enough to town to see steady traffic. Nearly everything is traditional, from a handful of easy classics like East Slab and The Owl to harder jamming such as The Umph Slot. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.11, with 5.10 the most common, and several multi-pitch lines suit newer leaders. A walk-off down either side of the top brings you back to the base. Its sunny exposure makes it a popular winter option.
co_dome_the_2.approach: A short hike from the road: cross the footbridge over the creek, bear right along the aqueduct trail, then turn left up the path to the base of the slab.

co_whiskey_rocks_north.blurb: A small granite outcrop in the Goose Creek and Molly Gulch country of the South Platte, popular with crack climbers and offwidth fans. Most of what is here is crack boulder problems, mostly easy to moderate, plus some trad lines and a few bolted routes. Whiskey Crack, Sleep, Barley Made It, Cheddar Business Bureau and Gouda Company are the favorites. The cracks climb with real physical effort and precise technique, and the rock is hard on skin, so bring tape. The approach is only a few minutes, which makes it an easy stop alongside the other domes nearby.
co_whiskey_rocks_north.parking_note: Follow the gravel Forest Road 211 toward Molly Gulch for about four miles, then pull off at the wide spot with trees on the left, just before the road climbs and curves left.
co_whiskey_rocks_north.approach: Walk uphill from the pullout to the obvious pile of rocks, a few minutes at most.

co_bear_canyon_bouldering.blurb: A bouldering zone in the central Flatirons, reached from the NCAR end of Table Mesa Drive and the trail up Bear Canyon. It holds around three dozen problems, all boulders, spread across a wide range of difficulty: the middle of the pack is V3 to V5, with a good number of V6 and V7 and a few V9s such as Amalgamation. Flake Roof and Tears Overhang are well-known lines. The setting is wooded and quiet by Boulder standards, and spring and fall tend to be the best seasons. Bring pads and expect to hike to reach the blocks.

co_county_seat.blurb: A compact cluster of boulders and a ridge crest of hard Dakota sandstone on the Tin Cup Hogback just outside Golden. The west side leans out slightly, while the east side stands more like a small flatiron. Problems tend to be either very easy or quite hard: a lot of VB and V0, then a stretch from V6 up to V9. Hogback Arete, Chorizo, Finders Keepers and Smiling Traverse are the ones to try. Most faces point west, so expect afternoon sun and cooler mornings. A few more small boulders sit a short way south along the ridge.
co_county_seat.parking_note: Use the T-Rex lot beside the I-70 road cut; park at the back of it, where the ridge trail begins.
co_county_seat.approach: Walk the ridge trail north from the T-Rex lot; the boulders sit directly on the path.

co_terrain_boulders_aka_droegerland.blurb: A scattering of large boulders in the trees at the base of the southern Flatirons, tucked away from the busier Boulder bouldering. Holds are varied, with slopers, crimps, pockets and flakes, and many of the problems are highballs, so bring several pads and a spotter. Most lines fall between V1 and V5, with a few hard ones up to Tower of Power at V10. Spewbacca, Plush and What About Bob? are good places to start. The forest and the Flatirons give plenty of shade on warm days. The hike in takes a while, which keeps the crowds down.
co_terrain_boulders_aka_droegerland.approach: From the Shanahan trailheads, join the Mesa Trail and walk to the rolling ridge; the boulders sit along its south side. Plan on most of an hour each way.
co_terrain_boulders_aka_droegerland.parking_note: Park along the road below the North Shanahan trailhead off Lehigh. That trail is busy, so some climbers instead use quieter pullouts on the south side of the hill near the South Shanahan trailhead.

co_hidden_valley_wall.blurb: A quiet granite cliff in Unaweep Canyon, farther along the trail than Sunday Wall and Fortress Wall. Almost all of it is traditional crack climbing, with most lines between 5.8 and 5.10: 5.9 is the largest group, and 5.10 comes close behind. Obe Won Canobe, Gorilla in Manilla, Illusions, Made In the Shade and Padawan are the standouts. Crowds are light, and the setting is pleasant. Spring and fall are generally the best seasons in the canyon, and the walk-in gives a nice warm-up.
co_hidden_valley_wall.approach: Follow the marked trail from the base of Sunday Wall past Fortress Wall and on to Hidden Valley Wall. Descend by walking off or rappelling.
co_hidden_valley_wall.parking_note: Pull off on the north side of Highway 141 at the pullout below Sunday Wall, a bit over two miles west of Divide Road, and take the trail from there.

co_north_gym_the.blurb: A short stretch of east-facing limestone at Shelf Road, between The Gym and The North End. The climbing is nearly all bolted and steep, with few easy outings: most routes fall at 5.11 to 5.13, and a handful of 5.10s break it up. Power Milk & Bagels is a favorite at that grade, with The North Gym and Who Left the Fridge Open? at 5.12a. Many first bolts are high, so a stick clip helps. It catches morning sun and goes into shade later, which suits warm days. The middle of the wall stays cooler than the south end.
